articles.title: A job that changed me: I mulched city parks in the dead of winter – I was not cut out for manual labour or working with family
articles.summary: My brother said I was terrible at mulching; he was right. But before tearing up my contract, he imparted some words of wisdom. In early 2020 in Canberra, I left my job in human resources.
body: By the time winter rolled around, it was Covid lockdowns. I had grown a scruffy beard and turned my bedroom in my mother’s house into a man cave, complete with empty beer cans, a TV blaring sport and a glowing gaming setup in the corner.

I had two issues: I needed money, and my mother wanted me out of the house. Fortunately my brother had recently launched a landscaping business, which had won a tender to mulch parks throughout Canberra, and he needed a workforce.

I offered my brother my landscaping CV, which included mowing Mum’s lawn and trimming the occasional hedge. I was hired, and joined a ragtag team which included an ex-sports physio, a former Canberra Raiders rugby player and a former plasterer. So while most of Canberra worked from home, we were sent out to empty parks.
Every day at 5am, we would pile into a filthy Toyota HiLux, pick up a skid steer loader – essentially a forklift with a bucket – and drive to a park we’d been designated for the day.
points: My brother said I was terrible at mulching; he was right.
But before tearing up my contract, he imparted some words of wisdom.

articles.title: Alessandro Michele designs for the dancefloor at Valentino’s Paris show
articles.summary: Italian designer plays with ‘idea of glamour in the wrong way’ in collection of see-through gauzy fabrics and mis-buttoned blazers. Alessandro Michele is the Italian designer who, during his seven year tenure as creative director at Gucci, made maximalism a meal ticket for the brand.
body: His challenge now is to bring the same hot sauce to Valentino. He’s been in the top creative job for just 30 months but time moves fast in fashion and he’s already rolled out 10 collections and four catwalk shows. At Paris fashion week on Sunday afternoon, he ticked off show number five.

A series of satin bustier tops paired with knee-length skirts opened the show. Some skirts were almost see-through in gauzy fabrics. Some came smothered in glimmering beads or trimmed with feathers or both.

The show may have been held at the Sainte-Geneviève library but these were clothes made for the dancefloor. The debauched partying mood dominated menswear too, with creased trousers and silky boxers peaking out above their waistbands and mis-buttoned double-breasted blazers. Michele said he liked playing with “the idea of glamour in the wrong way”.

The reaction to Michele at Valentino has been mixed. In a turbulent luxury market, its revenue declined 15% to €1.12bn in 2025. Michele’s opulent outlook has been slightly out of step with fashion’s vanilla era. However, the reign of quiet luxury is quietly coming to a close; “personality dressing” is on the rise and Michele is poised in the wings.
points: Italian designer plays with ‘idea of glamour in the wrong way’ in collection of see-through gauzy fabrics and mis-buttoned blazers.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Poppy the curious, clever dog – who searches for missing people
articles.summary: A beloved family pet, she is also the best employee ever, brilliant at her rescue work. If everyone could be more like Poppy, the world would be a better place. When we picked up a nine-week-old black labrador from a couple just outside Callander, Scotland, I had no idea that she would soon be an…
body: Poppy and our team of dogs look for missing people. My colleagues and I then provide any medical assistance needed. She is trained to search without needing to smell someone’s scent from an item such as clothing. During training, we hide our volunteers along the riverbank, in the woods, beside lochs and canals, and set the dogs off. They have to find the people and come back. Poppy’s curious nature has served her well. She loves the undergrowth, sniffing about and finding things.

She has been involved in a couple of searches, including one for a missing army veteran in the Scottish Borders, which, unfortunately, turned into a body recovery. She was also tasked with going up to Inverness to help find a missing child in the woods who, thankfully, was found by the police.
Poppy is the best employee. When she has her search jacket on, she knows she is going to look for people and the difference is apparent: she changes from family pet mode to working dog mode.

articles.title: Chicago’s Muhājir Honors the Spice Route with Flame-Grilled Food From Across the World
articles.summary: Chefs Zubair Mohajir and Jacob Dela Cruz debuted a new restaurant that explores culinary cultures across Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia this summer. Muhājir opened with a wood-fired menu that’s meant to be shared, an exciting change of pace for Mohajir and Dela Cruz whose previous…
body: Prep starts with breaking down a rare halal duck for the Duck Numidian dish, a 920-year-old recipe from southern Spain that they’ve been workshopping for years. The duck wings and neck are cooked down for the duck jus on the side, while the duck legs will become a confit folded into duck rice alongside the dry-aged duck breasts. The breasts hang over the fire right before service, before they are finished in the oven. Dips and shattas from around the world, using ingredients that range from cream cheese to fava beans, are served alongside papadam and roasted focaccia as a starter.
Watch the kitchen team at Muhājir cook everything from whole fish to beef cheeks over a huge fire in this episode of Now Open.

articles.title: Paris, Le Soir! Inside the Chicest Fashion Parties of the Season
articles.summary: You hardly thought everyone went home after the runway wraps, did you? Beyond the collection unveilings, the Spring 2027 season has seen no shortage of parties popping off across Paris. Here’s Vogue’s fly-on-the-wall look at who’s out and about—and why…
body: For a certain millennial cohort, Alexa Chung is the dictionary definition of an It girl—and now they can continue to lift ideas from the mood board fixture’s outfit repertoire thanks to her new co-designed collaboration with Reformation.

A few days before the capsule went live, Chung rallied the troupes for a night at beloved le Marais neighborhood watering hole, Le Saint-Gervais. Indulging in Caviar Kaspia and taking turns on the karaoke mic were the likes of Princess Olympia of Greece, Lila Moss, Amelia Dimoldenberg, Isabella Massenet, Pixie Geldof, Connor Ives, and Chung’s partner Tom Sturridge, who all hung out until late as the soirée spilled onto the side walk. Rounding out the transatlantic guest list were former Ref collaborators Camille Rowe and Camille Charrière, too.

“Paris Fashion Week is almost like summer camp in a way,” Jonathan Simkhai told Vogue at the intimate dinner he hosted at Red Katz for his nearest and dearest. “It’s always so exciting, seeing everyone, what they’re wearing and what people are excited about.”

articles.title: 5 Underrated Halloween Towns Across the US
articles.summary: Some are abandoned Gold Rush boomtowns; others are rife with haunted history. All are worth skipping Salem for.
body: I’ve always been a sucker for spooky season. My childhood consisted of watching scary movies with friends, being fascinated by ghosts and ghouls, and happily disappearing down rabbit holes about witch trials, haunted places, and the stranger corners of American history. Halloween is the perfect excuse for people like me who enjoy leaning into the mystery and having a little fun along the way—especially those of us in the Northeast, who get to enjoy the holiday alongside crisper weather and shorter days. If you ask me, it's the perfect time of year. So, why not make a trip out of it?
Read on for the best Halloween towns across the US to celebrate the season.

Bodie is what happens when a Gold Rush boomtown disappears and then refuses to put up a front for tourists. High in California ’s eastern Sierra, the road into Bodie State Historic Park winds past a lonely cemetery and into what was once a lawless mining town of around 10,000 people and nearly 60 saloons. Today, you can walk these same dusty streets and peer through the windows of homes, hotels, shops, a church, and a schoolhouse that are still in the same condition as when they were abandoned in the early 20th century.
points: Some are abandoned Gold Rush boomtowns; others are rife with haunted history.
If you ask me, it's the perfect time of year.

articles.title: The Couple Wed in an 18th-Century Hacienda Set Among Agave Fields and Golden Hills in Jalisco
articles.summary: Schuyler Ebersol and Clementina Davila exchanged vows in a historic hacienda, blending Mexican and American traditions throughout their wedding weekend.
body: In November 2012, Schuyler Ebersol spotted an Instagram photo of his future wife, Clementina Davila, standing next to his cousin. He was immediately smitten. “For years at family gatherings, the same question came up: Why hadn’t I been introduced to her,” Schuyler says, adding that he thought she looked like “an angel.” Nearly five years later, that same cousin noticed the two were both living in Charlottesville, Virginia, so she finally set them up on a dinner date.

“Clementina called her on the way to the restaurant to ask how to pronounce my name,” Schuyler recalls with a laugh. The two hit it off, and the date went on for hours. “We discovered we had both originally gone to college to be architects, both harbored a dream of moving to New Zealand despite never having been there, and both were obsessed with space,” Schuyler says. After the date, he called his sister and said he’d marry Clementina the next day if he were crazy enough to ask.
points: Schuyler Ebersol and Clementina Davila exchanged vows in a historic hacienda, blending Mexican and American traditions throughout their wedding weekend.

articles.title: A Birder’s Guide to Cape May, New Jersey
articles.summary: Cape May, New Jersey is on most birder bucket lists for a reason—it's perfectly situated to spot birds migrating for the season. Come for the incredible bird spotting, stay for the absolutely charming seaside town.
body: If you’re reading this, you probably like birds. And while there are many reasons to visit Cape May, New Jersey—it’s a charming coastal town described by a friend as “a mix between the towns in Practical Magic and the Gilmore Girls ” while we were there—it’s also beloved by birders for special for one very specific reason: its location.

Cape May is geographically positioned as the perfect rest stop for birds that are either heading south for the winter or north for the summer. There, you can see thousands of rare birds as they migrate—I was able to identify 25 different species during a two-hour stroll, and that was during a major rainstorm.

So if the city is on your birder bucket list, consider this your sign to visit while the Atlanta Flyway is hot (i.e., between the months of September and November for the fall migration and May for the spring migration). This fall, the bird is the word—just ask Matthieu Blazy, whose spring 2027 collection for Chanel, presented at Paris Fashion Week on October 5, featured light-up avian sculptures hanging from the ceiling of the Grand Palais.

articles.summary: Dua Lipa! Ayo Edebiri! Pedro Pascal! Photographer German Larkin gets up close and personal with all of the stars at Chanel in Paris.
body: Chanel and Paris Fashion Week go hand-in-hand like a fresh baguette and butter. It’s always one of the buzziest (if not the buzziest) shows of the week, and tonight, designer Matthieu Blazy’s unveiling of his latest collection— spring 2027 —was certainly no different.

The front row, meanwhile, was as exciting as the catwalk: A-listers such as Nicole Kidman, Pedro Pascal, Ayo Edebiri, Dua Lipa, Marion Cotillard, Alexa Demie, and more all showed up for the affair (wearing their finest Chanel duds, naturally).

And when there’s a star-studded VIP list, Vogue knows who to call: We enlisted photographer German Larkin to document all of the buzziest names in attendance. (Larkin also documented the Gucci show back in Milan.) Below, scroll on for exclusive sightings from Chanel’s spring 2027 show.
